solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Understands right to wear pants

indicators.note: a garment is worn around the wearer, so the letter for right goes inside the word for pants

parts.note: to pant is to gasp for breath, so pants gives gasps

explanation.surface: Someone sees the sense in a man's right to wear trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like trousers but is the verb, as in breathing hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp an idea is to understand it; a third-person verb matches the clue's form.

clue.text: Rescue dog with no tail

indicators.note: the last letter of the dog breed is cut off, its tail docked

parts.note: a retriever is a gundog breed

explanation.surface: A dog is saved from trouble, though it has lost its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrieve something is to recover or rescue it from a bad place.

clue.text: They'll give you a leg-up

parts.note: a leg-up usually means help in a career, but here it is literal: the loops a rider's feet rest in, used to climb into the saddle

explanation.definitionFit: Riders put their feet in these metal loops hanging from a saddle to mount and ride a horse.

clue.text: Study the score, express resignation and walk

parts.note: a sigh is the sound of weary acceptance
to tread is to walk or step

explanation.surface: A musician looks at the music, sighs in defeat and leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight-reading is playing music at first sight straight from the written notation.

clue.text: Germany is bound, say, to show a lack of belief

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

indicators.note: say signals that the word for bound is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: bound means tied up, trussed

explanation.surface: Germany feels obliged to express doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: To distrust is to doubt someone or lack faith in them, the verb sense matching 'show'.

clue.text: Politically motivated CD?

parts.note: CD looks like a compact disc, but it is the abbreviation for corps diplomatique, the body of ambassadors and envoys

explanation.definitionFit: The body of foreign diplomats posted to a capital is abbreviated CD, seen on their car plates.

clue.text: Destroyed hut after turning up pictures

indicators.note: after places the hut at the end, following the turned word
in a down clue, turning up reads the word for pictures from bottom to top

parts.note: pictures as a whole are art
a shed is a small hut

explanation.surface: A hut is wrecked after someone finds pictures inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trashed has been wrecked or ruined, a slang sense of destroyed.

clue.text: Mismatched diamonds, say, pinched by nude criminal

indicators.note: being pinched means being squeezed between, so the card group sits inside the anagram
criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters of nude are rearranged

parts.note: diamonds is one example of a suit in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A naked thief is caught with a stolen haul of diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diamonds, say' is an example standing for its class: diamonds is one of the four suits in a pack of cards, and 'criminal' scrambles the nude around it.
explanation.definitionFit: People unsuited to each other are a poor match, so mismatched is a synonym.

clue.text: Medicine container and cruet for disposal

parts.note: a tin is a metal container

indicators.note: for disposal suggests being broken up and got rid of, so the letters of cruet are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tin and a cruet set are put out with the rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A tincture is a medicine made by dissolving a drug in alcohol.

clue.text: Hang prints in order to cover grub, oddly

indicators.note: covering something wraps around it, so the rearranged letters go round the picked letters
in order suggests being sorted out, so the letters of prints are rearranged
oddly takes the odd-numbered letters, first and third

explanation.surface: Prints are arranged to hide some food.
explanation.definitionFit: To string someone up is to hang them, a phrasal verb for execution by rope.

clue.text: Dates and marmalade spread over nougat — originally plum

indicators.note: originally takes the starting letter of each of the six words before it

explanation.surface: A list of sweet treats spread out, ending with a plum.
explanation.definitionFit: A damson is a small dark purple variety of plum.

clue.text: Party animal sent back for words to music

parts.note: Lib is short for Liberal, a political party

indicators.note: sent back reads the animal's name from right to left

parts.note: an otter is a river animal

explanation.surface: A party-loving creature is returned for the lyrics of a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the text of an opera or musical, the words set to its music.

clue.text: Scrimping and scraping means half ot them split

indicators.note: a slip for 'half of', which takes the first two of the four letters of them

parts.note: a rift is a split or crack

explanation.surface: Penny-pinching drives a couple apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ot' is a typo for 'of': the first half of 'them' is TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrift is careful economy, the habit of saving money and avoiding waste.

clue.text: Set homework and read after revision

parts.note: prep is British school slang for homework

indicators.note: revision changes the order, so the letters of read are rearranged

explanation.surface: A teacher assigns homework and reading after a revision lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: Prep is British boarding-school slang for homework done in the evening, and 'after revision' rearranges the word read.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set is ready, the same as prepared, both past participles.

clue.text: Energy (and power) is firm friend of a bishop

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
P is the symbol for power
Co is short for company, a firm
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: Energy, power and a firm friend all belong to a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Episcopal is the adjective relating to bishops, from the Greek word for overseer.

clue.text: Contrary view on head of finance's charges

indicators.note: in an across clue, on places the reversed piece after the letter
head of takes the opening letter of finance
contrary means the other way round, so the verb for view is reversed

parts.note: to view is to see

explanation.surface: Someone takes the opposite view of the finance chief's charges.
explanation.definitionFit: Fees are payments charged for a service, a plural synonym.

clue.text: Foreign Office reacts badly is the prediction

parts.note: FO is the abbreviation for the Foreign Office, the UK foreign ministry

indicators.note: badly suggests things going wrong, so the letters of reacts are rearranged

explanation.surface: A forecast that the Foreign Office will react poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecast is a statement of what is expected to happen, such as the weather.

clue.text: Get out of botched EU caveat

indicators.note: botched means messed up, so the letters of EU caveat are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone escapes a poorly drafted European Union condition.
explanation.definitionFit: To evacuate a building is to leave it or clear it out.

clue.text: Panel discussion is about return of jobless

indicators.note: return means the run is read backwards
the run of letters lies about, across, the words panel and discussion

explanation.surface: A panel discusses the return of the unemployed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone idle has no work, the same as being out of a job.

clue.text: At home mainly healthy worker gets medication

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, so its final letter goes

parts.note: hale means healthy, as in hale and hearty
the worker ant is a crossword staple

explanation.surface: A worker stays home, fit for the most part, and takes some medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhalant is a medicine breathed in, as for asthma or congestion.

clue.text: The French covered in buzzing flies must be dead

indicators.note: covered in means wrapped by, so the French article goes inside the anagram
buzzing suggests a swarm moving about, so the letters of flies are rearranged

parts.note: les is the French plural word for the

explanation.surface: A corpse covered in buzzing flies must be dead.
explanation.walkthrough: The definite article here is plural French, not the singular le or la; 'buzzing' rearranges the flies around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lifeless shows no sign of life, the same as being dead.

clue.text: Dependency with no source of cash is a plus

indicators.note: with no means a letter is taken away from the word for dependency

parts.note: an addiction is a dependency

indicators.note: source of gives the opening letter of cash

explanation.surface: Getting over an addiction without money is a bonus.
explanation.definitionFit: An addition is something added, a plus or bonus.

clue.text: Conveyance supplied with a new Irish penny?

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh form, so the letters of Irish are rearranged

explanation.surface: A new Irish coin is used to pay for transport.
explanation.definitionFit: An airship is a vehicle, a means of conveyance through the air.

clue.text: Call for more heart, chasing points

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so the heart comes after the points

parts.note: E and N are two compass points, east and north
the core is the heart of something

explanation.surface: A crowd demands more heart after a points defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: An encore is an audience's call for a performer to come back and play more.

clue.text: Plant rotation for the most part — so be it!

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a cycle is a rotation, a repeated turn
amen means so be it, said at the end of a prayer

explanation.surface: A gardener accepts crop rotation for the most part with a resigned 'so be it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyclamen is a flowering plant with upswept petals, often grown indoors.

clue.text: A right of reply about route creates indifference

parts.note: a path is a route

indicators.note: right of takes the right-hand, final, letter of reply

explanation.surface: Giving someone a right of reply on a route plan only meets apathy.
explanation.walkthrough: The blog reads Y 'about' PATH, but in the grid Y follows PATH, so 'about' is best read as a link meaning concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathy is a lack of interest or feeling, the same as indifference.

clue.text: Material spiked is put back

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric, a material
a spiked drink has been laced with alcohol or a drug

explanation.surface: Fabric that has been spiked is returned.
explanation.definitionFit: Something replaced has been returned to its place, the same as put back.

clue.text: Spring in lock giving illegal entry

indicators.note: in puts the spring inside the lock of hair

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: A spring in a door lock lets in an intruder.
explanation.definitionFit: Trespass is entering land or property without permission.

clue.text: Most recent play without wingers before international

indicators.note: before places the middle letters ahead of the match
wingers are players on the flanks, so the outer letters of play are removed

parts.note: a test is an international match in cricket or rugby

explanation.surface: A team's latest play lacks wide men ahead of an international.
explanation.walkthrough: A test match is an international cricket or rugby game.
explanation.definitionFit: The latest is the newest, the most recent one.
